title: Exposition of a New Theory on the Measurement of Risk
venue: Econometrica (English translation of the 1738 Latin original)
question: Why won't anyone pay much to play a game whose expected payout is infinite?
changed: People value wealth by a concave utility, logarithmic in his example: the root of risk aversion and of growth-optimal betting.

title: Portfolio Selection
question: Why diversify, and how much of each asset should you hold?
changed: Choose portfolios by mean and variance: covariances make diversification computable, and the efficient frontier is born.
assumed: Investors care only about the mean and variance of one-period returns; inputs are known.

title: Safety First and the Holding of Assets
question: How should you invest if your goal is to avoid disaster?
changed: Minimize the chance of falling below a floor, which with mean and variance alone gives a Sharpe-like ratio: mean-variance found independently.

title: A New Interpretation of Information Rate
question: How much should a gambler with an edge bet to grow wealth fastest?
changed: Bet to maximize expected log wealth; the growth rate equals the information rate of the gambler's private wire.
assumed: Known odds and probabilities, repeated bets, no limits on fractional betting.

title: Liquidity Preference as Behavior Towards Risk
question: Why hold cash when bonds pay more?
changed: Separation: every investor holds the same risky mix plus cash, and risk tolerance only sets the split.

title: Optimal Gambling Systems for Favorable Games
venue: Proceedings of the Fourth Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability
question: In what precise sense is the Kelly bet optimal?
changed: The log-optimal strategy asymptotically outgrows any essentially different strategy and reaches any wealth goal fastest.

verified.note: Berkeley Symposium proceedings (1961) have no DOI; a 1962 technical report version does.

title: Lifetime Portfolio Selection under Uncertainty: The Continuous-Time Case
venue: The Review of Economics and Statistics
question: How should a long-lived investor consume and invest when trading continuously?
changed: Dynamic programming in continuous time: with constant relative risk aversion, hold a constant fraction (μ − r)/(γσ²) in stocks.

title: How to Use Security Analysis to Improve Portfolio Selection
question: How should a manager with some stock-picking views combine them with the market?
changed: Hold the market plus an active portfolio weighted by alpha over residual variance; the appraisal ratio measures the gain.

title: The fundamental law of active management
question: Where does an active manager's information ratio come from?
changed: IR ≈ IC × √breadth: skill per bet times the square root of the number of independent bets.

title: The Markowitz Optimization Enigma: Is 'Optimized' Optimal?
question: Why do practitioners distrust mean–variance optimizers?
changed: Optimizers maximize estimation error: they overweight assets whose means are overestimated.

title: Global Portfolio Optimization
question: How do you get sensible weights out of an optimizer when your views are partial?
changed: Start from the equilibrium returns implied by market weights and blend in views with Bayesian confidence.

title: The Effect of Errors in Means, Variances, and Covariances on Optimal Portfolio Choice
question: Which input errors hurt an optimized portfolio most?
changed: Errors in means cost roughly ten times more than errors in variances, and twenty times more than errors in covariances.

title: Risk Reduction in Large Portfolios: Why Imposing the Wrong Constraints Helps
question: Why do no-short-sale constraints often improve out-of-sample risk?
changed: A long-only constraint acts like shrinking the covariance matrix: wrong in theory, helpful in practice.

title: A well-conditioned estimator for large-dimensional covariance matrices
question: How do you estimate a covariance matrix when assets are many and days are few?
changed: Shrink the sample covariance toward a scaled identity with an optimal, data-driven weight.

title: Optimal Versus Naive Diversification: How Inefficient is the 1/N Portfolio Strategy?
question: Do optimized portfolios beat equal weights out of sample?
changed: Fourteen models fail to beat 1/N consistently; estimation windows would need centuries to win.

title: The Properties of Equally Weighted Risk Contribution Portfolios
question: What portfolio gives every asset the same share of risk?
changed: Formalized risk parity: it sits between minimum variance and 1/N and needs no expected returns.

label: López de Prado 2016
title: Building Diversified Portfolios that Outperform Out of Sample
question: Can portfolio construction avoid inverting an unstable covariance matrix?
changed: Hierarchical risk parity: cluster assets by correlation, then allocate top-down by inverse variance.

title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
question: Should exposure fall when volatility rises?
changed: Scaling factors by inverse recent variance raises Sharpe ratios and alphas, because volatility moves more than expected return.
